significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) conditional invariance: changing structure while retaining the "SAME enzyme" preserves the interaction signal, whereas a "DIFFERENT enzyme" metabolic bypass abolishes it, with enzyme-consistent steering providing additional causal evidence. This establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and an internal mechanism, and it fixes expected outcomes for new matched substitutions rather than merely showing that CYP identity is decodable; the FDA's 2020 guidance on CYP-mediated drug interactions confirms that enzyme inhibition, induction, and substrate status are operational determinants used in clinical DDI assessment. The hypotheses are determinate, and a verified negative would rule out shared-CYP computation as the causal basis of the tested models' judgments and undermine their use on structurally atypical pairs, although it would not by itself prove which surface correlation replaces it. After substituting away the shared-enzyme/bypass double dissociation, the broad scientific-representation topic would not merit this score, so the score comes from the claim-specific relation rather than the topic.

reach.justification: The claim names reusable handles: the "Shared-Enzyme-Beyond-Structure Index," "Bypass-vs-Same-Enzyme Causal Asymmetry," a "mechanism-based failure predictor," and the design rule that screening "must be gated by explicit metabolic-pathway checks" when the mechanism test fails. These can be used ex ante to audit or gate a model before relying on its DDI predictions, giving model evaluators, pharmacovigilance teams, and DDI-screening practitioners an action window rather than only explaining an observed error afterward. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction survives as a transferable ordering—bypass swaps should cause a larger signal drop than same-enzyme structural swaps—and the hypothesis asserts this across medical-language, chemistry, and molecule-text foundation-model classes, though not beyond CYP-mediated pharmacokinetic DDIs. Topic substitution removes these auditing quantities and the predeployment gating rule, so the reach is attributable to this claim rather than to scientific foundation-model interpretability generally.
